How to do itCable Chest Press

Back position

Right
SPINE NEUTRAL
Wrong
LOW BACK ARCHED

Right: Staggered stance, spine neutral, handles at nipple height.

Wrong: Lower back arched.

Stand with one foot in front of the other, feet planted.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Locked elbowsThe elbows lock straight at the front of the press.
Press2 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Grip

Single handles, neutral grip, just outside shoulder width. Press straight ahead, pushing through the palms.

Keep your wrists lined up with your elbows.

Common handling mistakes

  • Locking the elbows

    Fix: Extend your arms without locking the elbows.

  • Arching the lower back

    Fix: Keep your spine neutral and brace your abs.

  • Jerking the body, too heavy

    Fix: Choose a weight you can press with the body still.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your chest, front shoulders and the backs of your arms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

Standing presses load the trunk to keep you stable.

If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou are arching your back.

    FixKeep your spine neutral and brace your abs.

  • Usually meansYou grip much wider than shoulder width, or flare your elbows.

    FixKeep your elbows at a 45-degree angle.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set both pulleys at chest height with single handles.

  2. 2

    Stand a foot or two from the cables, a handle per hand.

  3. 3

    Step into a staggered stance, feet planted.

  4. 4

    Handles just outside shoulders, elbows just below 90 degrees, wrists over elbows.

  5. 5

    Brace your abs and glutes, spine neutral, shoulders down.

Risks and when to stop

  • Wide grips and flared elbows stress the shoulder, a common injury site in lifting.
  • Too much weight costs form and raises injury risk. Add weight in small steps.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

Back pain

Pain, numbness, tingling or weakness in both legs? Numb genitals or anus? Bladder, bowel or sexual changes? Chest pain? Serious accident? Get emergency help now. Sudden severe or fast-worsening pain? Hot, cold, shivery or unwell? See a doctor today.

No better in a few weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itMachine Pullover

Set the seat so your shoulders sit just below the machine's pivot.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back archesThe lower back arches away from the pad.
  2. Head off padThe head pulls forward off the pad.
Pull2 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Grip

No grip: open hands on the bar, fingers extended. Push with your elbows.

Common handling mistakes

  • Back arching off the pad

    Fix: Keep your back and head on the pad.

  • Arms off the pads first

    Fix: Feet on the bar first, then lower the stack with your legs.

  • Too much weight

    Fix: Lower the weight until you feel your lats.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this along the sides of your back.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansArching puts too much pressure on your lower back.

    FixKeep your back on the pad.

  • Usually meansTense shoulders let tension build up in your neck.

    FixRelax your shoulders down.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat so your shoulders are just below the machine's pivot.

  2. 2

    Fasten the belt, back flat on the pad, feet on the bar.

  3. 3

    Push the foot bar down, arms on the pads, then feet off.

  4. 4

    Pull the bar down to your belt. Hold it there a moment.

  5. 5

    To finish: feet on the bar, arms off, legs lower the stack.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arching the back puts too much pressure on the lower back.
  • Too much weight makes the lats harder to feel.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itMachine Crunch

Arm pull

Right
ABS CURL
Wrong
ARMS PULL

Right: Elbows held bent, the abs curl the trunk.

Wrong: Arms doing the pull while the trunk stays upright.

Spine curl

Right
SPINE CURLED
Wrong
HIP HINGE

Right: Spine curled, ribs coming toward the pelvis.

Wrong: Torso hinging at the hips without curling the spine.

Hips back

Right
HIPS BACK
Wrong
HIPS SLIDE

Right: Hips against the seat back, shins on the roller.

Wrong: Hips sliding forward off the seat back.

Keep your hips pressed against the back of the seat.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Arms pullThe arms drag the handles down.
  2. Trunk uprightThe trunk stays upright and the spine does not curl.
Crunch2 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Grip

Hold the handles in both hands. Start the crunch with your abs, not your arms.

Common handling mistakes

  • Pulling with the arms

    Fix: Start the crunch with your abs.

  • Using too much weight

    Fix: Lower the weight to protect your back.

  • Letting the stack rest

    Fix: Keep tension. Return without letting the stack rest.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your stomach.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansHinging at the hips shifts work to the hip flexors.

    FixCurl your ribs toward your pelvis.

  • Usually meansToo much weight can strain the back.

    FixAvoid excessive weight.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat to a comfortable height and choose the weight.

  2. 2

    Sit with your hips pressed against the back of the seat.

  3. 3

    Push your shins against the padded roller and tighten your abs.

  4. 4

    Hold the handles in both hands.

  5. 5

    Breathe out as you crunch. Don't strain your neck.

Risks and when to stop

  • Too much weight can strain the back.
  • Lower back pain? This machine works the hip flexors hard, so take care.

Back pain

How to do itLow-to-High Cable Fly

Trunk position

Right
TRUNK UPRIGHT
Wrong
LEANING FORWARD

Right: Trunk upright, staggered stance, abs braced.

Wrong: Leaning forward over the front foot.

Set the handles low, between knee and hip height.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows bendYour elbows bend deeply, turning the fly into a press.
  2. Becomes a pressBending the elbows more than slightly turns the fly into a press.
Close2 s
Hold1 s
Open2 s
Look closer

Grip

Single handles, palms facing each other at the front. Keep your wrists straight, in line with your forearms.

Common handling mistakes

  • Leaning forward, often too heavy

    Fix: Lower the weight and keep your trunk upright.

  • Bending elbows into a press

    Fix: Keep the slight elbow bend the whole rep.

  • Hands going past the armpits

    Fix: Stop opening at armpit level.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your upper chest, under the collarbones.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou are leaning forward, often because the weight is too heavy.

    FixLower the weight and keep your trunk vertical.

  • Usually meansYou are leaning forward.

    FixLower the weight. Keep your trunk vertical.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set both handles low, between knee and hip height.

  2. 2

    Take a handle in each hand. Staggered stance, trunk upright.

  3. 3

    Brace your abs. Don't arch your low back.

  4. 4

    Choose a weight you can lift without leaning forward.

  5. 5

    Choose a weight that lets you keep a soft elbow bend.

Risks and when to stop

  • Leaning forward raises stress in the shoulder joint.
  • Cable chest work loads the shoulder more than bench pressing. Keep joints stable.
  • A soft elbow bend and a short range keep strain off the shoulder.

How to do itHigh-to-Low Cable Fly

Trunk position

Right
TRUNK UPRIGHT
Wrong
TIPPED FORWARD

Right: Trunk vertical as the hands meet below the chest.

Wrong: Trunk tipped forward toward the hands.

Keep your trunk vertical, with no lean toward the hands.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hands crossYour hands cross past each other at the front.
Close2 s
Hold1 s
Open2 s
Look closer

Grip

One single handle in each hand, held firmly. Keep your wrists straight, in line with your forearms.

Common handling mistakes

  • Leaning forward

    Fix: Lower the weight and stand tall.

  • Arms behind or handles crossing

    Fix: Stop at the armpits going back. Let the hands just meet.

  • Torso moving toward the hands

    Fix: Keep the trunk still and let the arms move.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your chest.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansLeaning forward raises stress in the shoulder joint.

    FixLower the weight and stand tall.

  • Usually meansYou are arching your low back.

    FixBrace your abs.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set both handles at about the top of your head.

  2. 2

    A handle in each hand. Staggered stance, trunk upright.

  3. 3

    Brace your abs and keep your low back from arching.

  4. 4

    Pick a weight you can move without leaning forward.

  5. 5

    Sweep the arms down first, then in, in a wide arc.

Risks and when to stop

  • Leaning forward raises the stress in the shoulder joint.
  • Arms behind the body or crossing handles risks the shoulder and the hands.

How to do itSmith Machine Squat

Foot position

Right
FEET AHEAD
Wrong
FEET UNDER BAR

Right: Feet a few inches ahead of the bar, heels down.

Wrong: Feet directly under the bar, knees far forward.

Set your feet a few inches in front of the bar, not under it.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Feet under barYour feet are right under the bar, so your knees travel far forward.
  2. Knees far forwardYour knees push far past your toes.
Lower3 s
Drive up1 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, hands just outside your shoulders. Elbows under the bar, chest lifted.

Keep your wrists neutral.

Common handling mistakes

  • Feet directly under the bar

    Fix: Move your feet a few inches in front of the bar.

  • Knees caving in

    Fix: Reduce the weight and reset. Knees in line with the toes.

  • Rounding or over-arching the back

    Fix: Brace and keep your chest forward. Use a manageable weight.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your thighs and your glutes. Stop just short of locking your knees.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansPoor back posture puts more stress on your lower back.

    FixBrace and keep your spine neutral. Use a manageable weight.

  • Usually meansNot the normal dull pain 12 to 24 hours later.

    FixStop the workout at once. Don't train through the pain.

  • Usually meansThe bar on your neck puts pressure on a vulnerable area.

    FixStop, rack the bar, then move it onto your upper traps.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the bar just below shoulder level.

  2. 2

    Set the stops just below squat depth. Test with a light rep.

  3. 3

    Step under, bar across the upper traps, not the neck.

  4. 4

    Feet shoulder-width, a few inches in front of the bar.

  5. 5

    Hands outside the shoulders. Brace, then rotate the bar off the hooks.

Risks and when to stop

  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • Missed rep? Let the stops catch the bar, or rack it any time.
  • Smith loads differ from free-bar loads. Add weight in small steps.

How to do itSmith Machine Shoulder Press

Place the bench so the bar just clears your nose.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows flare wideYour elbows flare out wide, level with your shoulders.
  2. Level with shouldersYour elbows sit out in line with your shoulders, not in front of them.
Lower2 s
Press2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, palms forward, wider than your shoulders. Thumbs wrapped round the bar.

Bar low on the heel of your palm, so your wrist does not bend back.

Common handling mistakes

  • Elbows flaring wide

    Fix: Keep your elbows in front of your shoulders.

  • Back arching off the pad

    Fix: Press your upper back into the pad, brace, start light.

  • Elbows locking at the top

    Fix: Stop just short of full arm extension.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your front and side shoulders. Lower until upper arms are about parallel to the floor.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansAn excessive back arch.

    FixPress your upper back into the pad.

  • Usually meansFlaring the elbows wide.

    FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Bench at about 70 degrees. The bar should just clear your nose.

  2. 2

    Set the safety stops just below the lowest point of the press.

  3. 3

    Sit back, feet flat, upper back pressed into the pad, core braced.

  4. 4

    Grip wider than shoulders, thumbs wrapped. Rotate the bar off the hooks.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Bar passes your face: it should just clear your nose. Set stops, wrap thumbs.
  • Heavy presses send blood pressure very high, partly from holding your breath.
  • Shoulder injuries are common in lifting.

How to do itHip Abduction

Full range

Right
COMFORTABLY WIDE
Wrong
SHORT RANGE

Right: Legs opened comfortably wide.

Wrong: Knees opened only a little.

Set the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Short rangeYour knees open only a little before the legs come back.
Push out2 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Grip

Hold the side handles for stability and brace your trunk.

Common handling mistakes

  • Jerking the weight

    Fix: Keep your upper body still. Lower the weight.

  • Weight too heavy for form

    Fix: Lower the weight.

  • Incomplete range

    Fix: Open the legs to a full, comfortable range.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your outer hips and the sides of your glutes.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe machine may not be set to fit you.

    FixLine your knees up with the pivot.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot.

  2. 2

    Back on the pad, feet on footrests, pads snug on outer thighs.

  3. 3

    Pick a weight you can move without losing form.

  4. 4

    Hold the handles and brace your trunk.

  5. 5

    Push your legs out, hold briefly, then return slowly.

Risks and when to stop

  • A machine that doesn't fit you can strain the hip.
  • Too much weight spoils form.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itHip Adduction

Start width

Right
LIGHT STRETCH
Wrong
TOO WIDE

Right: Legs open to a light inner-thigh stretch.

Wrong: Legs forced wide into a deep stretch.

Start only as wide as a light stretch in the inner thighs.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Spread too wideThe legs are spread into a deep, forced stretch at the start.
Squeeze2 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Grip

Hold the side handles. Keep your back flat against the pad.

Common handling mistakes

  • Swinging the legs together

    Fix: Squeeze and return slowly.

  • Starting in a deep stretch

    Fix: Set a narrower start: a light stretch only.

  • Weight too heavy for form

    Fix: Choose a moderate weight.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your inner thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe start stretch is too deep.

    FixSet a narrower start.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Back against the pad, feet on the footrests, hold the side handles.

  2. 2

    Set the thigh pads on your inner thighs, just above the knees.

  3. 3

    Set the start width to a light stretch, not a deep one.

  4. 4

    Pick a moderate weight and check the selector pin is secure.

  5. 5

    Squeeze, pause briefly, then return slowly, keeping tension.

Risks and when to stop

  • Avoid an excessive stretch at the start.
  • Acute hip or groin injury? Don't use this machine.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itMachine Lateral Raise

Shoulders down

Right
SHOULDERS DOWN
Wrong
SHRUGGED

Right: Shoulders down, elbows at shoulder height.

Wrong: Shoulders hiked up toward the ears.

Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the pivots.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Above shouldersYour arms rise above shoulder level, elbows higher than your shoulders.
Raise2 s
Hold1 s
Lower3 s
Look closer

Grip

Hold the handles, pads just above the elbows. Lead with the elbows.

Keep your wrists neutral.

Common handling mistakes

  • Swinging the body up

    Fix: Lower the weight and lift without momentum.

  • Shrugging the shoulders

    Fix: Keep your shoulders down. Go lighter if needed.

  • Too heavy for shoulder height

    Fix: Lower the weight.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the sides of your shoulders.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansShrugging lets the traps dominate.

    FixKeep your shoulders down. Go lighter.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivots.

  2. 2

    Sit with your back on the pad, feet flat on the floor.

  3. 3

    Arms on the pads, just above the elbows. Hold the handles.

  4. 4

    Pick a lighter weight than you think.

  5. 5

    Lower slowly, stopping before the stack rests.

Risks and when to stop

  • Swinging the body to finish a rep can lead to injury.
  • It is easy to choose a weight that is too heavy.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itRear Delt Fly

Elbow bend

Right
FIXED BEND
Wrong
BENT SHARPLY

Right: Slight, fixed elbow bend as the arms open.

Wrong: Elbows bent sharply as the arms open.

Keep your chest against the pad for every rep.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Shoulders shrugYour shoulders shrug up toward your ears as the arms open.
Pull1 s
Hold1 s
Return3 s
Look closer

Grip

Neutral grip, palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent. An overhand grip also works.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rushing the reps

    Fix: Slow down your rep tempo.

  • Momentum, chest off the pad

    Fix: Lower the weight and keep your chest on the pad.

  • Too heavy, traps take over

    Fix: Lower the weight.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the backs of your shoulders.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansOther upper-back muscles are doing more than the rear delts.

    FixShorten the range. Stop at the shoulder line.

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the machine's handles to the reverse-fly position.

  2. 2

    Set the chest pad and handles so you grip at shoulder height.

  3. 3

    Chest pressed on the pad. Sit tall, neck neutral, eyes ahead.

  4. 4

    Take the handles with a neutral grip, elbows slightly bent.

  5. 5

    Don't let the weight stack rest between reps.

Risks and when to stop

  • Sharp pain at the front of the shoulder means stop.
  • Going too heavy lets the traps take over.
